name: Hardcore Heaven
caption: DPW's own World Tag Team Champions as of the fed's Motor City Madness PPV, 21 July 1996; the fed's own roster sheet names its two members as X-Treme and Hardcore.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5/4/96 roster sheet and its 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet ('Hardcore Heaven 7/21/96 to').

identity.note: Shares a bare name with hardcore-heaven-obw, a singles wrestler inducted into OBW's own Hall of Fame (class of 2008) -- a different era, a different roster shape (a singles wrestler vs. this wing's tag team), and no document ties the two. Recorded distinct on the no-auto-merge default.

name: The New Negaforce
caption: DPW World Tag Team Champions by the fed's own late-January 1997 newsletter (Malachite and Jedite), sharing a name with — but not the same lineup as — the fed's own 1996 tag team Negaforce.

tenures.source: The fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast (defeats Extreme Justice, led by Drac 'The Raven' Dravin and Terry 'Shotgun' Storm, 1 January 1997) and its own 31 January 1997 newsletter, billing 'DPW World Tag Team Champions - The New Negaforce (3-0)'. No document recovered in this wing's own record shows how the belts passed from the fed's 1996 champions, Hardcore Heaven.

name: Los Gringos Locos
caption: Won a tag match on DPW's own return card from Minneapolis, 29 November 1997, after beating the same opponents 'to oblivion' the week before.

tenures.source: The fed's own Saturday Night FEAR broadcast, 29 November 1997: defeats The Health Heroes at 4:16 in the show's first match.

name: The Health Heroes
caption: Lost DPW's own return-card opener to Los Gringos Locos, 29 November 1997, on a roster its own announcers called 'already depleting.'

tenures.source: The fed's own Saturday Night FEAR broadcast, 29 November 1997: lost to Los Gringos Locos at 4:16.

name: The Midnight Riders
caption: Awarded a forfeit win on DPW's own return card, 29 November 1997, when their scheduled opponents had already left the fed.

tenures.source: The fed's own Saturday Night FEAR broadcast, 29 November 1997: awarded a forfeit win over Macabre and B. Astard, who 'left the DPW.'

name: Boston Battalion
caption: A WCWF-era tag team (Joel "The Mouse" McGrath and Dan Kelly, neither minted here) inducted into DPW's own Hall of Fame in its first roster sheet, on the strength of a two-time WCWF World Tag Team Championship run the fed's own writers carried over as history.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5/4/96 roster sheet, in a dedicated 'DPW Hall of Fame' section: a two-time WCWF World Tag Team Championship reign, a rivalry with Made Out of Steel carried from the WCWF into the CVWF and EWA, and management by 'Doug McGrath' of a stable called 'the Firm.'
